chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Kindi, from Ahmad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Mithammi, from Anbasa Al-Abid, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Frequent laughter removes the water (dignity/luster) of the face.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Al-Sadiq peace be upon him)
key_terms.مَاءِ الْوَجْهِ: Water of the face (metaphor for dignity, luster, or freshness)

ai.seo_question: What is the effect of excessive laughter on a person's dignity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links excessive laughter to the loss of 'water of the face' (ma' al-wajh), a metaphor for the spiritual luster and dignified presence (haybah) cherished in Shia ethics. This narration, situated within the chapter on humor, warns against uncontrolled mirth that undermines solemnity and self-respect, reflecting the broader tradition of balancing joy with gravity. The teaching emphasizes that while laughter is permissible, its excess can erode the inner light that manifests outwardly.
